answer: Weekly, each identity must answer 100 hidden prompts seeded by a crystal nonce; independent verifiers hash every reply and plot correlation as a ridge across the ledger. Identities whose vectors match above 0.95 are merged, however busy the wharf of submissions. One shared model therefore counts once, so 1,000 Sybils gain nothing unless an attacker fine-tunes 1,000 truly distinct models at about $400 each ($400,000) and keeps them uncorrelated. Trade-off: honest agents on a popular base model risk false merging.
